points.description: States that the main advantage of passing arguments by reference is that no copy of the argument is made when the function is called, so large data structures are not copied. Equivalent wording (e.g. 'avoids duplicating large data', 'saves memory and time by not copying the data') earns the mark. Stating only a vague benefit such as 'it is more efficient' without linking it to avoiding copies does not earn the mark.

rubric.notes: The model answer contains a single idea: passing by reference avoids copying large data structures when calling a function. Full marks go to a student who states this idea in their own words, with the copying and large data both present or clearly implied. No marks go to a vague efficiency claim with no link to avoiding copies, or to an incorrect advantage such as safety or ease of use presented as the main one.
